texts.text: Using the MultiSensor data on high GOR wells

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The example trend below shows a standard ESP with gas separator running in a well with high free gas content. The well is horizontal and 'burps' large slugs of gas, which upset the ESP operation. The only way to control these slugs was to quickly choke back the wellhead pressure as discharge pressure was seen to drop off (thereby compressing some of the discharge pressure of the pump. This caused the pump to run in severe up thrust both from the lock of back pressure and also the low gravity of fluid being pumped.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: This example shows the effect of a well being produced with an intake pressure below bubble point. It can be seen that the pressure trend oscillates as the volume of gas at the pump intake increases. The oscillation occurs as the pump ∆ P decreases due to the lighter density free gas. As the intake pressure rises gas is forced back into solution and the pump delta increases again, producing a lower intake pressure. The total oscillation period is approximately 3 minutes in this case.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Trend vibration data has shown that certain ESPCP operating frequencies can produce high vibration readings.
texts.text: Trend vibration data has shown that certain ESPCP operating frequencies can produce high vibration readings.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Adjusting the operating frequency by a small amount up or down can significantly reduce the vibration value, reducing the mechanical stress on the downhole completion. The plot also shows the effect on motor temperature as the frequency is reduced. Power consumption of the pump is proportional to the frequency of operation; therefore reducing the speed of the pump reduces the load on the motor.
